assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves with controlled pore architectures and active sites underpins industrial catalysis and separations (cracking, methanol-to-olefins, emission control). The field shows how structure determines function, with clear originality in organic structure-directing agents, new framework types and tailored active sites. Its importance is high and long-lasting, though the work is a broad body of research rather than one discovery.
assessment.attribution: Corma (design of catalysts and zeolites, industrial translation), Davis (synthesis strategy, framework design, catalytic concepts) and Zones (organic structure-directing agents, new frameworks such as SSZ-13 and its use in NOx control) are decisive and complementary. Tsapatsis and Yu are important but arguably later or more specialized contributions. Credit is plausible for three but contestable against other strong zeolite scientists outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of independent confirmation and large industrial impact. Recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as one coherent discovery or a broad research area
Allocation among several equally strong contributors to zeolite synthesis and catalysis
My own field proximity means I must guard against over-weighting it

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiencies from a few percent to above 25 percent within about a decade, an unusually rapid and reproducible rise that has redefined photovoltaic materials research. The chemistry of composition tuning, defect tolerance and processing is rich and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell in 2009, Park produced the first solid-state, more stable device in 2012, and Snaith demonstrated high-efficiency planar and mesostructured devices that triggered the field. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis are also strong, so a three-person prize leaves out serious contributors.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed in many laboratories, but long-term operational stability, lead toxicity and commercial scale-up remain open. Recognition is timely, with some caution about durability.
uncertainties: Device stability and lead content may weigh against maturity
Contested credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis
Possible preference for a physics-oriented framing rather than chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base to another in genomic DNA without double-strand breaks, using engineered deaminase chemistry. This is an original molecular-engineering concept with rapid therapeutic uptake, including clinical trials, and a chemical-biology identity that fits the chemistry prize.
assessment.attribution: David Liu led the invention and is the clear central figure; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, requiring directed evolution of a new deaminase) were lead experimentalists. Kondo and Nishida independently developed a related deaminase-Cas system, which complicates priority. A single-person or Liu-centred prize is simpler, but three names are defensible.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is emerging and the method is widely used, but it is only about ten years old, so recognition could be somewhat early. Off-target and delivery questions remain.
uncertainties: Relation to the Cas9 genome-editing prize already awarded
Independent Kondo/Nishida work and trainee credit
Long-term clinical outcomes still unknown

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation via PROTACs and molecular glues exploits the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove proteins that are difficult to inhibit. It changes the concept of drug action, links to thalidomide mechanism, and has produced numerous clinical candidates.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced and developed the PROTAC concept, while Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, the structural and mechanistic basis for molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray and others contributed key advances, so the candidate is a compound discovery needing careful partitioning.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic basis is well supported, and clinical results are accumulating, although approval of a degrader drug is still pending. Moderately mature, slightly premature.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet
Different parts (PROTACs vs. cereblon glues) may need separate recognition
Heavy medicinal-chemistry content outside my own expertise

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from nano- and microcrystals with diffraction-before-destruction and time-resolved studies of reactions. It is a true enabling method, conceptually close to my own work on small crystals, and has delivered new structures of membrane proteins and photoreaction intermediates.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof of principle and the concept of diffraction before destruction, Fromme contributed the sample and crystal-delivery work with the first demonstrations, and Schlichting contributed time-resolved applications and instrument development. Hajdu is a foundational originator whose credit matters, and the allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed at multiple facilities; routine use is limited by beamtime access, and many structural results are incremental. Reasonably mature for recognition.
uncertainties: Relative importance versus cryo-EM and microED in practice
Facility access limits broad impact
Credit for Hajdu and many instrument developers

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase structure and mechanism describe the metalloenzyme that fixes nitrogen under ambient conditions, with the unusual FeMo-cofactor and its interstitial carbide. The crystallography is exacting and the problem is of fundamental and agricultural importance.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the key crystal structures of the MoFe protein and FeMo-cofactor, Einsle determined the central light atom as carbon at high resolution, and Seefeldt contributed mechanistic spectroscopy and biochemistry. Dean and Ribbe also made major biochemical contributions, so credit is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding steps are still debated, so the central question is not fully settled.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 reduction remains debated
Many credible contributors beyond three slots
Bioinorganic emphasis may be seen as less urgent than other candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (M41S, SBA-15, MCM-41) opened tunable large-pore materials and a general templating strategy used for catalysts, adsorbents and nanocasting. The conceptual originality is high and links to MOF and COF design thinking.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck discovered the M41S family at Mobil, while Stucky and Zhao developed SBA-15 and wide-ranging synthesis rules, and Ryoo developed carbon replication and ordered mesoporous carbons. Credit among the Mobil team and later academic groups is contested and difficult to partition.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and confirmed, but applications have not matched the early expectations and the discovery dates to the early 1990s, so impact may be seen as having plateaued.
uncertainties: Priority between Mobil inventors and Japanese and academic groups
Practical impact less than for zeolites
Allocation among six listed names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Computational descriptors such as the d-band model and scaling relations connect surface electronic structure to catalytic activity, enabling rational catalyst design for ammonia synthesis, hydrogen evolution and CO2 reduction. The concept is influential and predictive, and has been validated experimentally.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the dominant figure for the d-band descriptor and computational screening; Scheffler contributed first-principles surface science and Rossmeisl worked on the electrochemical descriptors. Hammer and others, not listed, also contributed to the d-band picture, so I treat the credit as partly incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and verified in many systems, though accuracy of DFT and the limits of scaling relations are active questions. Mature enough.
uncertainties: Contribution of researchers not in the credited list
DFT accuracy limitations
Whether it is theory-led enough to fit the prize as a discovery
